resolution.title: [ctrmgrd] Fix flaky iptables test by mocking DNS resolution
resolution.description:
#### What I did
Fixed intermittent build failure in `ctrmgr_iptables_test.py::TestIPTableUpdate::test_table` (#23432).

#### How I did it
1. **Mocked `socket.gethostbyname`** — the test was calling real DNS resolution which is environment-dependent. On build machines with DNS hijacking or NXDOMAIN redirection (common in corporate/Azure environments), invalid hostnames like `www.google.comx` resolve to a proxy IP instead of failing, causing unexpected test results.

2. **Replaced `www.google.comx` with `host.invalid`** — the `.invalid` TLD is reserved by [RFC 6761](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6761) and guaranteed to never resolve, providing an extra safety net.

3. **Added explicit `ret` assertion to test case 3** — previously test case 3 (`www.google.com`) only checked `post_rules` via regex `.*` but never verified the return value. Now it asserts the deterministic mock IP.

#### Root cause analysis
The reported error was:
```
AssertionError: assert '<IP>:3128' == ''
```

Test case 4 passes `ip="www.google.comx"` expecting `_get_ip()` → `socket.gethostbyname()` to fail (return `""`). But on ARM64 build machines where DNS resolves typo domains to a proxy/redirect IP (<IP>), the hostname resolves successfully, causing `iptable_proxy_rule_upd` to return `"<IP>:3128"` instead of `""`.

#### How to verify it
```bash
cd src/sonic-ctrmgrd
python -m pytest tests/ctrmgr_iptables_test.py -v
```

The test now passes deterministically regardless of the build environment's DNS configuration.

#### Which release branch to backport
None

#### Description for the changelog
Fixed intermittent ctrmgrd iptables test failure caused by environment-dependent DNS resolution.

Fixes #23432
